subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should the macOS updater contract treat repeated/no-op manual update jobs as a runtime repair target, an explicit refusal/no-op path, or only a documented recovery case?
rationale: Current code can repair some launchd service states, but deciding whether to add duplicate-job suppression, no-op short-circuiting, or stronger detached handoff semantics changes the update lifecycle contract for existing macOS users.

options.title: Keep Open And Define The Updater Contract
options.body: Use this issue to decide and validate the manual-update job cleanup/dedupe behavior alongside the open launchd update.run handoff work.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Move duplicate submitted-job cleanup, node skew, and update.run handoff semantics into separate canonical issues before closing this umbrella.

options.title: Accept Current Recovery Stack
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept the remaining manualupdate label gap and require users to use doctor/docs for future recovery evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep Open And Define The Updater Contract
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide and validate the manual-update job cleanup/dedupe behavior alongside the open launchd update.run handoff work.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent provided recent maintainer verification and correction on the managed update handoff recovery stack and has recent commits in the affected update/launchd path.
